text:
A $6.3bn exploit at the world's largest exchange, and the damage was far more contained than the headline suggests.

Our read this week is that the response is the story. Approximately $2.8bn of the stolen assets was rapidly frozen by Circle, Tether and other issuers, and Binance has reportedly replenished affected funds through its own reserves and insurance fund. The exploit represented a small part of Binance's $171bn in customer assets.

For allocators, the useful point is structural. Transparent on-chain infrastructure made it possible to trace and freeze stolen assets at speed, something that is much harder to do in opaque systems.

That is also why we argue for a common language for risk. Our report with Clear Street breaks DeFi exposure into chain, protocol and asset layers, so that an event like this can be located quickly: where did it sit, and what did it touch?

The full note is in this week's Weekly: [link]
